key_concepts: Solar energy is the primary driver of Earth's climate and weather.
Uneven solar heating due to Earth's curvature causes temperature differences.
Warm air rises and cool air sinks because warm air is less dense.
Wind is the movement of air from high-pressure to low-pressure areas.
Clouds form when rising water vapor cools and condenses onto condensation nuclei.

The Intertropical Convergence Zone is a low-pressure belt near the equator where trade win
The ITCZ shifts north and south with the seasons.
Monsoons are seasonal wind patterns that bring distinct wet and dry conditions.
Amihan brings dry, cool air to the Philippines, while Habagat brings heavy rainfall.
Global wind patterns include atmospheric circulation cells and trade winds.
The water cycle links evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.
